chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Salih al-Razi from Hamdan al-Diwani. He said: Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said:

Whoever visits me despite the distance of my abode, I will come to him on the Day of Resurrection at three stations so that I may deliver him from its terrors: when the books of deeds fly to the right and to the left, at the Path (Sirat), and at the Scale (Mizan).

key_terms.الصراط: Sirat — the bridge over Hellfire that all must cross on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.الميزان: Mizan — the Divine Scale upon which deeds are weighed
key_terms.زيارة: Ziyarah — the pious visitation of the shrines of the Prophet and Imams
key_terms.يوم القيامة: Day of Resurrection — the final judgment when all are held accountable

ai.seo_question: What reward does Imam al-Rida promise to those who visit his shrine?
ai.summary: In this hadith narrated in the shrine of Imam al-Rida (AS) in Tus, the Imam promises to personally intercede for his visitors at three critical junctures on the Day of Judgment. The three stations mentioned — the distribution of the records of deeds, the crossing of the Sirat bridge, and the weighing of deeds on the Mizan — represent the most terrifying moments of the eschatological process in Islamic belief. This tradition served to encourage pilgrimage (ziyarah) to the shrine of Imam al-Rida, particularly significant since the hadith was recorded in Tus itself.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. Ahmad b. Musa (rh) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi `Abdullah al-Kufi narrate to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Salih al-Razi from Hamdan al-Diwani. He said: Al-Rida (as) said:

Whoever visits me despite the distance, I will meet him in three places on the Day of Resurrection so that I may deliver him from its terrors: (1) when the Book is given to his right and left hand, (2) at the Path, and (3) at the Scale.
